items.prompt: At Library A, 24 of 80 workshop participants finished a project. At Library B, 30 of 120 finished. Which library has the higher observed completion percentage?
options: A: 30%, compared with B: 25%.
B: 30%, compared with A: 25%.
Both: 30%, despite different group sizes.
B, because six more participants finished.

items.prompt: A club's participation rate rises from 40% to 50%. Which statement correctly separates the percentage-point change from the relative percentage increase?
options: 10 percentage points; a 10% relative increase.
10 percentage points; a 25% relative increase.
25 percentage points; a 10% relative increase.
25 percentage points; a 25% relative increase.

items.prompt: Service Cedar reports 3 late deliveries, and Service Elm reports 6. No total delivery counts are given. What can these counts alone establish about their late-delivery rates?
options: Cedar's rate is half Elm's because its late count is half as large.
Elm's rate is higher because it has three more late deliveries.
The rates cannot be compared without the total deliveries for each service.
The rates are equal because both services have some late deliveries.

items.prompt: Five fictional waiting times, in minutes, are 4, 5, 5, 6 and 30. What are their arithmetic mean and median?
options: Mean 5 minutes; median 10 minutes.
Mean 6 minutes; median 5 minutes.
Mean 10 minutes; median 6 minutes.
Mean 10 minutes; median 5 minutes.

items.prompt: In the ordered waiting times 4, 5, 5, 6 and 30 minutes, replace only 30 with 90. What happens to the mean and median?
options: The mean rises to 22 minutes; the median stays at 5 minutes.
The mean stays at 10 minutes; the median rises to 22 minutes.
The mean rises to 22 minutes; the median rises to 17 minutes.
The mean stays at 10 minutes; the median stays at 5 minutes.

items.prompt: Twelve students read an average of 5 pages each. Three other students read an average of 20 pages each. What is the average across all 15 students?
options: 5 pages per student.
8 pages per student.
12.5 pages per student.
20 pages per student.

items.prompt: On the same 100-point test scale, Group A's mean moves from 40 before a workshop to 60 after it. Group B's mean moves from 70 to 80. What are the observed increases in group means?
options: A: 10 points; B: 20 points.
A: 20 points; B: 20 points.
A: 20 points; B: 10 points.
A: 40 points; B: 70 points.

items.prompt: Two methods are used by beginners and experienced participants. Method A succeeds for 20 of 80 beginners and 18 of 20 experienced participants. Method B succeeds for 2 of 10 beginners and 72 of 90 experienced participants. Which statement matches these counts?
options: A has the higher success rate overall and within each experience group.
B has the higher success rate overall and within each experience group.
The methods have equal success rates within both experience groups.
A is higher within each experience group; B is higher when all participants are pooled.

items.prompt: One group records the values 10, 10, 10 and 10. Another records 0, 0, 20 and 20 in the same units. Which comparison is correct?
options: Their means are equal, but the second group's range is larger.
The second group's mean is larger, but their ranges are equal.
Both their means and their individual observed values are equal.
The first group's mean is larger because none of its values are zero.

items.prompt: A newsletter invites readers to reply voluntarily about a new bus timetable. Of the 200 people who reply, 180 say it is useful. What does the calculated 90% directly describe?
options: The share of all city residents who find the timetable useful.
The share of these respondents who say the timetable is useful.
The share of nonrespondents who would find the timetable useful.
The chance that a different voluntary poll will also report exactly 90%.

items.prompt: Eighty volunteers are randomly assigned, 40 each, to interface A or B. They perform the same task, and completion time is recorded for everyone. What does random assignment principally help accomplish?
options: Make the volunteers a random sample of all possible interface users.
Ensure every baseline trait is exactly balanced in this particular run.
Prevent baseline traits from systematically deciding the assigned interface.
Ensure that any difference in task time cannot arise through chance variation.

items.prompt: Students choose whether to join a study group. Those who join average 75 on a test; those who do not average 65. No earlier achievement or other differences are measured. Which conclusion is supported by this design alone?
options: Joining the study group raises every student's score by exactly 10 points.
Repeating this voluntary comparison with more students would remove all confounding.
The lack of random assignment proves that study groups cannot affect scores.
The participants scored higher here, but the comparison alone does not establish that joining caused the difference.
